## Item 42 — More avatar motifs + a gentle onboarding pick-your-symbol step

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-22. **Model: Sonnet, low–medium effort.** No schema/Room change (stays **v27** — the `avatar_motif` column + Room v27 already shipped in [v1.6.7.md Item 3 Leg 1](v1.6.7.md#item-3--profile--couple-photo-upload-pulled-from-post-v1-horizon-9)). No grill needed — straight pattern-follow, mirroring the already-shipped Currency onboarding step almost line for line.
- **Request:** Alvin, from a conversation about profile-icon discoverability — the motif-avatar picker (Item 3 Leg 1) only lives in Settings → Profile ([ProfileScreen.kt:157](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/ProfileScreen.kt#L157)), so a new user never sees it unless they go looking. Asked to (a) add more symbols to the catalog and (b) gently ask new users during onboarding "what symbol represents you best?" instead of leaving it undiscovered.
- **Change:**
  - [MotifAvatar.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/MotifAvatar.kt)'s `AvatarMotif` enum: expand the free catalog (currently 8 — Heart/Leaf/Bloom/Sparkle/Wave/Crescent/Gem/Sprout) with more glyphs from the already-bundled `material-icons-extended` set (no new dependency), in the same soft/nature/couple-friendly register. Exact additions finalized during build. `MotifPicker`'s 4-wide chunked grid needs no change — it already works for any entry count.
  - New `feature/onboarding/presentation/OnboardingMotifScreen.kt` + `OnboardingMotifViewModel.kt`, mirroring [OnboardingCurrencyScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/presentation/OnboardingCurrencyScreen.kt) / [OnboardingCurrencyViewModel.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/presentation/OnboardingCurrencyViewModel.kt) exactly: reads the current user's `accentColor` (via `ObserveCurrentUserUseCase`) to tint the picker, renders the existing `MotifPicker`, persists instantly on tap via the existing `UpdateAvatarMotifUseCase` (same call `ProfileViewModel.onMotifSelected` already makes — no new use case). Plain "Continue" without tapping anything keeps the Heart default. Copy stays gentle/skippable, not a hard gate — matches the onboarding graph's established low-friction tone (Templates step is "fully skippable").
  - [OnboardingGraph.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/OnboardingGraph.kt): insert the new step between Welcome and Currency (Welcome → **Motif** → Currency → Pair → Templates); bump the four existing "Onboarding step X/4" doc comments to X/5 across `OnboardingWelcomeScreen`, `OnboardingCurrencyScreen`, `OnboardingPairScreen`, `OnboardingTemplatesScreen`.
  - `AvatarMotifTest.catalog_hasEightMotifsWithUniqueKeys` updated to the new count/key list (the other two tests iterate `entries`/fallback keys and auto-cover new additions).
  - **Does not touch:** the `avatar_motif` schema/column (already shipped), the Settings → Profile picker (unchanged — still where to change it later), or ADR-0014's accent-color pairing-flow logic.
- **Verify:** `./gradlew testStagingDebugUnitTest` + `assembleStagingDebug` green. On-device: fresh account through onboarding end-to-end — new step renders between Welcome and Currency, tapping a motif persists it (visible in Settings → Profile right after finishing onboarding), and tapping "Continue" without selecting anything keeps the Heart default. Pure Composable/ViewModel wiring — verified by running, matching the Currency step's own precedent.

## Item 43 — Employer reimbursement tracking / general Receivables & Payables module (idea, not booked)

- **Status:** IDEA — parked 2026-07-22, not booked to build. No model/effort chosen — needs a decision first.
- **Context:** Alvin asked whether the app covers "expenses reimbursable by my employer." Today it doesn't as a first-class concept — no counterparty/status field on `transactions`, and `partner_debts` doesn't generalize (its `borrower_id`/`lender_id` are both `users` rows inside a couple, not a non-app third party like an employer or friend). Current workaround: tag expenses with a "Reimbursable" category, log the payback as an Income transaction — no pending/settled tracking or running total like Partner Debt Tracker gives couples.
- **Why parked, not booked:** same problem shape as the personal-loans call already made (personal loans = notes + transactions, no V1 entity — see Product Decisions memory). A real Receivables & Payables module (reimbursements + personal loans + misc IOUs unified, with pending/settled status) would reopen that decision and is genuine new scope, not a mechanical build.
- **Next step if revisited:** run `/grilling` first — cross-cutting (new counterparty concept, new sync-ordered entity, touches the settlement-leg pattern from ADR-0019) — before anything here gets promoted to a real PLANNED item.

## Item 1 — Delete account: Play Console Data Safety web setup

*(originally booked in [v1.6.7.md](v1.6.7.md), held in [v1.6.8.md](v1.6.8.md), moved here 2026-07-22 when v1.6.8 became the widget-fix release — number preserved from v1.6.7)*

- **Status:** PLANNED, not started. **Non-code** — Alvin executes with Claude's guidance when he's ready. **No grilling needed** — this is compliance paperwork (a static page + a Play Console form field), not a design decision; every design call for account deletion itself was already made in [ADR-0045](../adr/0045-delete-account-hard-delete-rpc.md).
- **Request:** the in-app deletion RPC + client teardown shipped in [v1.6.5.md Item 6](v1.6.5.md#item-6--delete-account-play-policy-requirement-) (`9e0614e`+`22d7cc1`, on-device verified), but Google Play's Data Safety policy also requires two things that live outside the app: (1) a publicly reachable "Delete my account" web page, and (2) the Play Console → App content → Data safety form's account-deletion URL pointing at it. Both still pending, flagged as "Alvin, manual" in the v1.6.5/v1.6.6/v1.6.7 write-ups.
- **Guide (when we sit down to do it):** draft a static `delete-account.html` on the existing `alvinleyble.github.io/ipon-love-legal` GitHub Pages site (sibling to `privacy-policy.html`), describing the in-app self-service path (Settings → Profile → Delete account) and what gets removed (per ADR-0045 — full cascade, no retained data, immediate). Push it to the `ipon-love-legal` repo, then fill in the Play Console Data Safety form's deletion-URL field. No app code changes.
- **Verify:** page loads publicly at the URL; Play Console form saves without validation errors.

## Item 41 — Play Store screenshot refresh (Playful Pop reskin)

*(booked 2026-07-22 in [v1.6.8.md](v1.6.8.md), moved here 2026-07-22 when v1.6.8 became the widget-fix release — number preserved)*

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-22. **Model: Fable 5, low effort.** No schema/Room change. No grill needed — straight iteration of the existing render pipeline, not a new design.
- **Request:** Alvin — "since we reskinned, we'll need to update our screenshots in playstore." The v1.6.7 Item 8 "Playful Pop" redesign (`f570463`+the full Slice 6 rollout, [v1.6.7.md](v1.6.7.md) Item 8) changed the visual identity of every screen since the last screenshot set was rendered (v1.6.5 Item 22, `43f59c1`, Rose-dark captures on the pre-reskin M3 look).
- **Change:** re-run the existing pipeline in [assets/brand/playstore/](../../assets/brand/playstore/) — drop fresh raw captures (Rose, light+dark per the existing convention) into `assets/brand/phone-screenshots/` from the now-reskinned app, remap slide→screenshot filenames in `slides.css` as needed, re-render via `render.sh` (recipe documented in `assets/brand/README.md`). Reuses the same 8-slide Heart-Wallet brand-voice design system — no new slides, no copy changes, just re-capturing the underlying screens. Per [[playstore-screenshots-in-flux]], expect this to repeat again as more UI lands — republish to the same Artifact gallery path for review rather than standing up a new one.
- **Verify:** 8 Play-compliant 1080×1920 images regenerated, reviewed via Artifact gallery; Play Console upload stays Alvin's manual step (repo assets only, no app code/tests affected).
